questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, good academic opportunities and a different environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, there was much information and a bit overwhelming at times. There was a lot of forms to fill out but that is expected, and they give clear instructions on how to do it. If there was any problems, support was quick and very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Free taxi-service from airport to accomodation, orientation week to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: UniMelb offers many accomodations. I lived at Lisa Bellear House, which was about a 20 minutes walk from campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: University accomodation is very pricy, and not worth it in my opinion. It is a good place to meet new people in the beginning, but there will be a lot of events throughout the semester so its not really necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Way too expensive. My room was super small. There is also not a very big sense of community as most people that live there are other exhange students, and will only be staying for one semester. It's very different from Danish dorms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of paperwork, and a bit of a struggle to show I had the necessary requirements.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You fill out a form for every single subject, where you have to list the courses you have taken. Could be simplified by only requirering one list of all previous courses, too save some paperwork.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Support was quick and fast over mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just start looking at the courses early, and make sure you have the prerequisites.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found most of the courses to be very chaotic and not well structured. Professors and lectures were also not as enthusiastic as I am used to. It seemed they were sometimes a bit rushed and not very well prepared. Others were extremaly shy, would only read up from a Powerpoint or notesheet, and never look up.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say the level of courses are similar to KU, but as the course structure was very chaotic it was sometimes hard to know what excactly was the syllabus. Also, no courses used textbooks, but instead the lecturers own notes or just powerpoints, which was often less structured and educational than a normal textbook.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar lecturers. We also had tutorials (regnetimer), but it was not nearly enough time to finish the work for each week, and often only one TA for the whole class, so they didnt have enough time to help. Courses would have one hour every week or every other week, so often you could only ask one question (if you were lucky).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Theoretical Physics 3
Sub-atomic Physics
Elements of Quantum Computing
Electronic Dance Music Technique

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Theoretical Physics 3 was the best course. A fairly difficult course, but very interesting, good professors. Was the best strucured course, but still not very good as they didnt give an overview of what we where supposed to learn each lecture. 

Sub-atomic Physics is a horrible course, would not recommend to anyone. There was two professors, which are easily the two worst professors I have ever had. Extremely messy way of teaching, no structure whatsoever, no examples of how to do problems in lectures, no correspondance between lectures and problems in tutorials. Only one turorial every other week, which was not nearly enough. I had too learn all the syllabus by myself. It is some very interesting material, but sad it is taught in such a horrible way. 

Elements of Quantum Computing was very interesting. It was fairly easy, as there are a mix between physicists, mathematicians, computer scientist and finance students taking it. If you've had quantum mechanics before, the first 4 weeks is basicly recap. Then they start too teach you how the different quantum algorithms work, which I enjoyed a lot. They change professors often, and while some are good, some are pretty bad, but it was easy enough that it's possible to learn it by yourself. 

EDM Technique was I course I took to try something new. It's okay if you like EDM, but completalyi online so very anti-social. Would take something else if I had the chance.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is expensive, just buy a cheap bike.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: University accomodation is extremaly expensive you're better off trying to find a sharehouse.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the surfing-club and boxing club, very fun and good value for money.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bunch of different clubs too join, they're all fairly cheap and good value for money, would highly recommend joining one. There is a bunch of events for exchange students, especially in the beginning, great to join too meet people. There is a gym on-campus, its very good but quite expensive

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both the surfing- and boxing-club was very fun. The club for exchange students also hosts a bunch of events I would recomend going to.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Melbourne in general has a ton of events all the time. Keep a look out for concerts, DJs, plays etc. Many nice museums. You can rent a car and take day-trips (or overnight stays) to Philip Island, Torque (surfing), Great Ocean Road, St. Kilda beach (can also do public transport). After exams I spent a bunch of time doing a road trip along the eastcoast, highlights are Cairns (Great Barrier Reef diving is awesome), Brisbane, Byron Bay, Sydney, Kosciuszko National Park. Bring a tent and enjoy;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, very similar to western countries.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and events. Nobody knows anyone in the beginning, so its very easy to make friends!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really. One thing to be aware of is that there is a lot of drugs going around, and you will often be asked if you want something and you will see people openly do drugs at nightclubs etc, which can be uncomfortable.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very chill and laidback people, very friendy and generally love talking to strangers (in contrast to scandinavians). Say hi to people!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Spend your weekends wisely, do day-trips etc
Be open and try to meet as many people as possible in the beginning so you figure out who you vibe with.
Whatever you do, don't take enroll in sub-atomic physics.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont take sub-atomic physics.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends from all over the world, and seeing Australia, a very beatiful country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Saying goodbye to those friends. 
Also, my wallet is not in the best condition, but its worth it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Dont take sub-atomic physics.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
